tasks.instruction: Add an optional free-text note to invoices. Add a new migration for it (do not edit existing migrations) that keeps every existing invoice; invoices that never had a note have the note "". GET /invoices/<id> must include "note". POST /invoices accepts an optional "note". PATCH /invoices/<id> accepts "note" as well as the existing fields, and every later GET of that invoice, including one answered from the Redis cache, must show the change. Add or update tests for this.

Add POST /invoices/<id>/pay. Paying an open invoice marks it paid and queues an issue_receipt job, and the worker then records the receipt. Paying an invoice that is already paid returns HTTP 409 and queues nothing; an unknown invoice returns 404. The job queue delivers at least once, so the same job can arrive more than once: the worker must never record two receipts for one invoice. GET /invoices/<id> must show status "paid" straight after paying, even if the invoice was cached. Add or update tests for this.

Customer names are stored as free text on each invoice. Move them into their own table: add a new migration (do not edit existing migrations) that creates a customers table with a unique name, fills it from the existing invoices with one customer per distinct name, gives invoices a customer_id that references it, and drops the old invoices.customer column. Existing data must survive. The API must not change for clients: GET /invoices/<id> still returns "customer" as the name, and POST /invoices with a customer name reuses that customer or creates it. Also add GET /customers/<id>/invoices, which lists that customer's invoices. Keep seeding a new database working. Add or update tests for this.

Add GET /invoices to list invoices as JSON: {"invoices": [...], "next": <id or null>}. Each item has the same fields as GET /invoices/<id>, and items are in ascending id order. Query parameters: status=open|paid keeps only that status; customer=<name> keeps only that customer's invoices (exact match); limit=<n> caps the page size (default 20, at most 100); after=<id> returns only invoices with a larger id. "next" is the id of the last invoice on the page when more matching invoices exist beyond it, otherwise null, so a client pages by passing it as after. An unknown status, a limit that is not a whole number from 1 to 100, or an after that is not a whole number of 0 or more, returns HTTP 400. Add a new migration (do not edit existing migrations) with an index on invoices that covers status and id for this query. Add or update tests for this.

Add POST /invoices/<id>/void. Voiding an open invoice sets its status to "void" and returns the invoice. The database only allows the statuses open and paid today: add a new migration (do not edit existing migrations) so that it also allows void, still rejects any other status, and keeps every existing invoice. A paid invoice cannot be voided, and a void invoice cannot be voided again: both return HTTP 409 and change nothing. An unknown invoice returns 404. A void invoice is final: PATCH /invoices/<id> on it returns 409 and changes nothing. GET /invoices/<id> must show status "void" straight after voiding, even if the invoice was cached. Add or update tests for this.
